tiles.title: Designing an Experiment to Figure Out How the Servo Works

text:
Just like we did with the demo gripper, we want to figure out how the servo block works.

What we know is that it goes from 0%-100% rotation, but how can we control that movement?

Design a program that will help you figure out:

  1. How do you make the servo move to 100% rotation?
  2. Can you make the servo move to other angles? For example, 90%, or 45% rotation?
  3. If no, why not? If yes, how? Is there an amount between 0-100% rotation that it can't go to?

Just like last time, you might be asking "What is my program supposed to look like?"

You probably already guessed the response: there isn't just one way to make things work in programming!

Throughout these lessons, you will be developing strategies for designing and making new programs!

But you don't always have to make programs from scratch.

tiles.title: Try the Class Portfolio to Tell Jokes

text:
Try it! Try changing parts where it says "sort by" or "show for."

First, drag this tile over and write a joke.

Find another group's joke, and drag it into your workspace.

You might want to try clicking where it says "sort by" at the top of the "Class Portfolio" tab.

If you tried something and it didn't work, you can click on "Class Portfolio" again and it'll take you back.

Can you find the program you used to figure out what the demo gripper does?

Once you find it, work with your partner to think about how to change or improve it so that you can figure out what the servo does.

It might be a necessary change (e.g., to make it work for a new purpose), or it might be an improvement that isn't strictly necessary (e.g., to make it easier to use, or to make it better in some other way).
What change or changes will you make to your program so that you can use it to figure out what the servo does? (if you want, you can use a "sketch" tile to draw out your idea instead of writing it)
Why will you make that change/those changes?
You made a plan! Now time to enact it! Move on to the "Develop" tab!
